content.title: How To Watch the Utah Jazz Live Anywhere Without Cable 2026
content.text: Don’t miss a single note this season. The Utah Jazz are composing something new and you can stream every minute from your living room. With streaming services like Sling TV and Hulu, you’ve got a courtside seat from home. This year, the Jazz are leaning hard into youth and promise. Anchored by core pieces like Keyonte George, Walker Kessler, Isaiah Collier, Ace Bailey, Taylor Hendricks, and rising forward Kyle Filipowski, the team is auditioning tomorrow’s stars today. And the best part? Watching the Jazz at home is easier than spotting the Great Salt Lake on a map. + In this article How to stream Utah Jazz games You can watch Utah Jazz games using streaming services like YouTube TV, Sling TV, Hulu + Live TV, and more. Many of those include the national and regional channels needed to catch the games. Here's the breakdown of all the channels carrying Utah Jazz and what they show: ABC/ESPN: NBA Wednesday, some Friday national games, Saturday Primetime, Sunday Showcase, Christmas Day games, and the NBA Finals NBC/Peacock: Coast-2-Coast Tuesday double header, some Sunday Night Basketball games (affter NFL season), and Peacock NBA Monday Amazon Prime Video: Most Friday night games, Thursday night games (after NFL season), and select Saturday afternoon gamesNBA League Pass: Out-of-market games Related channels Price NBA League Pass All games not nationally broadcasted and not in your local region $16.99-$24.99/mo or $109.99-$159.99/season Amazon Prime Video Exclusive NBA games (Thursday nights, NBA Cup) Starts at $8.99/mo YouTube TV ABC, ESPN, NBC, NBA TV $67.99/mo for first three months, $82.99/mo after Hulu + Live TV ABC, ESPN, NBC $89.99/mo Sling TV ABC, ESPN, NBC $60.99/mo (need Orange + Blue) Fubo ABC, NBC, ESPN, NBA TV $48.99/mo for first month, $73.99/mo after DIRECTV Streaming ABC, ESPN, NBC, NBA TV, Regional sports $84.99/mo for first month, $124.99/mo after Peacock NBC Sports content, exclusive NBA games $10.99/mo Watching the Utah Jazz with YouTube TV Score a slam dunk with YouTube TV — one of the best services for streaming NBA games. Their base package price starts at $67.99/mo for first three months, $82.99/mo after and includes all of the channels needed to catch every game — ABC, ESPN, NBC, and NBA TV. Additionally, YouTube TV offers unlimited cloud DVR services so you can rewatch your favorite moments. For wallet-conscious fans, the price may seem on the higher end. That being said, the base YouTube TV package also allows for: Three simultaneous streams Six individual user accounts Access to 100+ live TV channels YouTube TV is compatible with most smart devices, including FireTV, Roku, and AppleTV. It also works on Google Chromecast, PS4/PS5, Xbox, and even Peloton. When factoring in cost, the ability for more users to stream content in addition to NBA games may make it a good fit for those who have households with varying interests. Watching the Utah Jazz with Hulu Hulu + Live TV is another excellent option for watching your favorite NBA team. Their “With Ads” packages start at $11.99/mo (with a three-day free trial). Subscribers gain access to over 85 live channels, including ABC, ESPN, and NBC. There’s an option to upgrade to $18.99/mo to remove ads from some of the Hulu services, but ads will remain in effect for ESPN+. Neither package offers NBA TV. The subscription also includes nine months of DVR cloud recording so you can rewatch on demand. Hulu + Live TV is easy to access on nearly any device and has an available add-on feature if you need additional screens. With an extensive on-demand library, Hulu + Live TV is a great choice for those who want both live sports coverage and other entertainment options. Watching the Utah Jazz with Sling TV Get off the sidelines and into the game with Sling TV’s affordable packages. Their Orange & Blue package starts out at $60.99/mo. For you to get full coverage (including NBA TV), you’ll need to add the Sports Extra package, bringing the total to $44.99/mo. Alongside its competitors, Sling TV also provides a cloud DVR feature, which is limited to 50 hours of storage (you can upgrade it to 200 hours for $5.00 a month). Watching out-of-market games Out of town? The Jazz can come to you from anywhere in the world with an NBA League Pass. But what about regionally blocked games? A VPN can keep you off the bench and still on your couch. For international fans living outside the U.S., NBA League Pass is the best option. You can live stream every game or watch it on demand. Subscribe to NBA League Pass NBA League Pass is one of the best ways to watch out-of-market NBA games. It’s the NBA’s official streaming service offering live games, replays, and more additional content than the basketball fans can handle. For $16.99 a month (or $109.99 per season), subscribers can watch live games that are not being aired on national networks or regional sports channels. For an even more immersive experience, the NBA League Pass Premium for $24.99 a month (or $159.99 per season) allows you to stream live games commercial free. Premium also allows you to download games directly to your device to watch whenever you want. Use a VPN Now, if you’re a die-hard NBA fan living outside of local broadcasting areas, you may experience regional blackouts. These can be super frustrating. It doesn’t help that streaming services also enforce geographic restrictions. This means you may not have access to certain games regardless of your paid subscription tier within that service. Thankfully, there is a workaround. By using a VPN to mask your location and bypass any restrictions, you’ll still be able to stream your games and stay in the game. A VPN (Virtual Private Network) works by rerouting your internet connection through servers in different cities or even countries. This makes it look like you’re browsing from somewhere else and hides your current location. By doing this, you gain access to geo-locked or blacked-out content. For local U.S. content, Surfshark is a great VPN option. Surfshark offers the most U.S. server access as well as fast and reliable connections. With a VPN, you can ensure you never miss a game, no matter where you are. FAQs How can I watch Utah Jazz games internationally? With NBA League Pass, you can stream as many Jazz games as you want. If you find yourself region-blocked, you can connect to a top VPN service. How can I watch the Utah Jazz without NBA League Pass? You can catch the Jazz on YouTube TV, Hulu + Live, or Sling TV and save your money. These services have you covered for every channel broadcasting every Atlanta Hawks moment. How can I watch the Utah Jazz without cable? You can stream from platforms like YouTube TV, Hulu + Live, and Sling TV, which offer access to the channels broadcasting NBA games. You can also use NBA League Pass. Bottom line Keyonte George and Lauri Markkanen are striking the right chords. Now the Jazz just need a little more harmony. If you’re outside of the Utah network, NBA League Pass and a VPN are your keys to staying in the action.
